findings.issue: Phase completion order is still internally inconsistent for same-root task tracking. It says to write phase-result before the phase commit and include it in that commit, but phase-gate requires a real commit record. A commit cannot contain its own final SHA, so the coordinator either writes an unknowable commit_sha before commit or updates phase-result after commit and leaves the worktree dirty, which the new gate rejects.
findings.recommendation: Define one executable order explicitly: commit implementation/evidence first, capture that SHA, write phase-result with that commit record, commit only tracking artifacts if task_tracking_root is inside the worktree, then run phase-gate accepting the recorded implementation commit as HEAD or HEAD^ under that documented two-commit shape.

findings.issue: Commit validation only checks whether any recorded SHA equals HEAD or HEAD^. It does not prove the commit record belongs to the current phase. A stale previous-phase commit at HEAD^ can satisfy file_changes after a new phase-result/tracking commit, letting the phase complete without a current-phase commit record.
findings.recommendation: Validate the commit record against the current phase identity and intended commit shape. At minimum require commit_records entries to include the current phase_id and accept HEAD^ only when HEAD is the tracking-artifact commit for the same phase; otherwise require HEAD.

resolutionSummary: Tests pass and the new schema/CLI coverage exists, but the phase-gate commit handoff is still not closed: docs describe an impossible same-commit SHA flow, and the gate can accept stale HEAD^ commit records.

findings.description: Spec describes or requires eliminating internal contradictions between field contracts or rule statements (cluster A: schema/contract terms + cluster B: conflict/contradiction/duplicate terms). Multiple conflicting schemas for the same entity cause silent drift — schema-drift blocking.
